name: Network Connection Type and Quality
description: The communication link between the UAV and the human operator can switch between distinct modalities (e.g., high-bandwidth 5G/Wi-Fi, 4G LTE, or low-bandwidth satellite fallback). This creates sharp, discrete steps in latency for transmitting images to the operator, leading to multimodal human analysis times. It is ranked first because network state transitions are typically discrete and have a massive impact on remote tasks.

name: Operator Multi-tasking and Queueing
description: Human operators often monitor multiple UAVs or perform other tasks. If the operator is immediately available, the response time is fast (first peak). If they are occupied, the image enters a queue, adding a distinct waiting time overhead (second peak). This queuing behavior naturally creates a bimodal distribution in human analysis times.

name: Onboard Resource Contention
description: The UAV's onboard computer runs multiple critical processes (e.g., flight control, path planning, SLAM/navigation, image classification). If the processor dynamically prioritizes flight safety during intensive maneuvers, the classifier is starved of CPU/GPU cycles, shifting its processing time into a significantly slower modal group.

name: Adaptive/Early-Exit Classifier Architecture
description: If the onboard classifier uses an adaptive neural network (e.g., early-exit or cascading architectures), easy-to-classify images exit at shallow layers (very fast peak), while ambiguous or complex images must pass through the entire deep network (slow peak). This architectural feature directly generates multimodal inference times.

name: Scene Complexity and Information Density
description: Highly complex environments (e.g., dense urban areas with many objects) take significantly longer for both humans to scan and onboard algorithms to parse (e.g., object detection bounding box generation). Simple environments (e.g., open sea or desert) are processed almost instantly, creating distinct time groupings based on the waypoint environment type.

name: Weather and Atmospheric Conditions
description: Adverse weather (fog, heavy rain, dust) degrades image quality. In clear weather, classification is fast. In poor weather, the human operator must spend extra time zooming, panning, or adjusting contrast to verify the image, while the onboard classifier might trigger fallback/retry routines, creating a distinct 'delayed' time group.

name: Operator Expertise and Experience Level
description: Human operators may have vastly different skill levels (e.g., highly experienced veterans vs. trainees). Veterans analyze images rapidly with high confidence, while trainees deliberate and double-check, resulting in two distinct peaks in human analysis time depending on who is on shift.

name: Thermal Throttling of Onboard Hardware
description: The onboard hardware (e.g., Jetson GPU) may experience thermal throttling when operating under high workloads or in hot climates. When throttled, clock speeds drop discretely to prevent damage, causing a secondary, much slower peak for onboard classification times.

name: Distance to Base Station
description: As the UAV flies farther from the ground control station, signal degradation leads to packet loss and frequent TCP/IP retransmissions. This causes transmission times to jump from a 'low loss' mode (fast) to a 'high retransmission' mode (slow).

name: Time of Day and Lighting
description: Daylight vs. nighttime/dusk conditions change image characteristics. Night/low-light images require longer exposures (causing motion blur) or infrared processing. For humans, glare and long shadows increase visual fatigue and decision-making time, creating distinct diurnal time distributions.

name: Image Resolution and Compression Level
description: The system may dynamically adjust image compression (e.g., raw TIFF vs. highly compressed JPEG) based on available bandwidth. Processing raw files takes longer both to transmit and to load/render on the operator's screen, while highly compressed files load fast but may cause human delays due to compression artifacts.

name: Operator Shift and Fatigue
description: The cognitive processing speed of human operators drops during long shifts or night rotations. Alert operators (start of shift) analyze images quickly, whereas fatigued operators (end of shift) exhibit delayed reaction and processing times, resulting in multimodal distributions.

name: UAV Flight State and Maneuvers
description: If the UAV takes an image while accelerating, turning, or battling high winds, the resulting motion blur or camera vibrations require the onboard image stabilizer or the human operator to wait/post-process the frame, dividing the times into 'stable flight' (fast) and 'unstable flight' (slow) modes.

name: Target Ambiguity
description: The specific objects of interest at waypoints might be highly distinct (e.g., a bright red vehicle) or highly ambiguous (e.g., a camouflaged object). Ambiguity causes both human operators to hesitate (seeking confirmation) and classifiers to require more iterations or alternative model pathways, producing a distinct 'uncertain target' time peak.

name: Ambient Temperature
description: Extreme ambient temperatures affect both the UAV's onboard cooling efficiency (inducing hardware throttling) and battery discharge rates. Although a physical factor, its effect is indirect compared to direct software/network state changes, placing it at the end of the ranking.
